3.1: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: holding the citta to one place uses buddhi’s power to fix (adhyavasāya, SK 23). Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.3.11 — yoga is ‘steady holding (dhāraṇā) of the senses’ — the very word; Ṛgveda 5.81.1 — the seers ‘yoke the mind’. Meaning: concentration is the Vedic yoking, applied to one point.
3.2: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: a single unbroken flow of pratyaya — buddhi taking one form continuously (SK 23, 36). Veda: Chāndogya Up. 7.6.1 — ‘meditation (dhyāna) is greater than thought (citta)’; Gītā 6.19 — ‘like a lamp in a windless place that does not flicker.’ Meaning: the flame stays still because nothing disturbs it.
3.3: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: buddhi so clear it shows only the object — SK 28’s bare seeing (ālocanamātra). Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 2.2.4 — ‘become one with it (tanmaya), like the arrow in the target’; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.23 — ‘becoming collected (samāhita), one sees.’ Meaning: the meditator disappears into what is seen.
3.4: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: saṃyama is a technical tool; Sāṃkhya’s nearest equal is SK 64’s ‘practice of the principles’. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.12 — the Self ‘is seen by subtle seers through a sharp, subtle intellect (agryayā buddhyā).’ Meaning: the three together make the intellect sharp.
3.5: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: prajñā’s light is the sattvic power of buddhi (SK 13: sattva illumines). Veda: Gāyatrī, Ṛgveda 3.62.10 — ‘may Savitṛ stir our intellects (dhiyaḥ)’. Meaning: Yoga answers the Gāyatrī’s prayer by its own effort.
3.6: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 22’s order of evolutes is climbed step by step. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 7 — Sanatkumāra leads Nārada from name upward, one stage at a time, to the infinite. Meaning: stages are not to be skipped.
3.7: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: inner in relation to the first five limbs, as SK 33 calls buddhi, ahaṃkāra and manas the ‘inner organ’ against the ten outer senses. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.10 — ‘beyond the senses are the objects, beyond the objects the mind, beyond the mind the intellect.’ Meaning: the practice moves further in.
3.8: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: even saṃyama is ‘outer’ to the seedless state — SK 65: puruṣa looks on but does not take part. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 1.1.4–5 — the lower knowledge includes even the Vedas; the higher grasps the imperishable. Meaning: the method is not the goal.
3.9: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 67 — saṃskāras of restraint gradually replace the old impetus of the wheel. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.3.11 — yoga ‘comes and goes (prabhavāpyayau)’; restraint must itself become a habit. Meaning: stillness is built moment by moment.
3.10: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: a calm flow arising from saṃskāra — prakṛti now serving release (SK 56). Veda: Chāndogya Up. 7.26.2 — ‘with firm memory, all knots are released.’ Meaning: what began as effort becomes the mind’s natural current.
3.11: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: rajas gives way to sattva (SK 13). Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.12 — the Self is seen by a one-pointed (agryā) intellect. Meaning: scattering decreases as focus increases.
3.12: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the same pratyaya arising and passing in sequence — buddhi like a steady lamp (SK 13, 36). Veda: Gītā 6.19 — the lamp in a windless place. Meaning: one-pointedness is when each moment repeats the last.
3.13: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 9 (satkārya) and SK 16 (the guṇas change ‘like water’ into many forms) — change is transformation of what already exists. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.1.4–6 — clay, copper and iron: one substance, many forms that are ‘only names’. Meaning: things don’t appear from nowhere; they change form.
3.14: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the dharmin that persists through past, present and future is SK 9’s cause in which the effect pre-exists. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.2.2 — ‘how could being come from non-being?’; 6.1.4 — clay is the reality. Meaning: the substance stays while its forms come and go.
3.15: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: different sequences give different results — SK 16’s water changing differently in different containers. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.3–4 — three deities combined in different proportions make the world’s variety. Meaning: order of change explains difference.
3.16: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: past and future exist in the cause (SK 9), so they can be known. Veda: Īśa Up. 8 — the Self ‘disposed all things rightly through endless years’; Ṛgveda 10.129 asks what existed before creation. Meaning: knowing the pattern of change opens past and future.
3.17: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: vikalpa (1.9) undone — word, meaning and idea pulled apart. Veda: Ṛgveda 1.164.45 — ‘speech is measured in four parts; three are hidden in secret, men speak the fourth’; Ṛgveda 10.71.4 — ‘one who sees has not seen speech.’ Meaning: the seers knew speech had layers the ordinary listener misses.
3.18: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 40 — the subtle body carries saṃskāras from birth to birth. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.2 — at death, ‘knowledge, deeds and past experience take hold of him.’ Meaning: the past lives that matter are stored in the present mind.
3.19: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: other minds are buddhis like one’s own (SK 18: many, alike in kind). Veda: Īśa Up. 6 — seeing all beings in the Self. Meaning: the same stuff of mind can be read in others.
3.20: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: one knows another’s state of mind, but not its object. Veda: Kena Up. 1.5–6 — what the mind cannot think, but by which the mind is thought. Meaning: knowing a thought is not knowing its support.
3.21: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 7 lists the causes of non-perception — invisibility is one of them, produced deliberately. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.12 — the Self ‘hidden in all beings does not shine forth’. Meaning: being seen depends on the meeting of light and eye.
3.22: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 67 — karma already in motion runs out like the potter’s wheel; karma not yet started can be read. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 6.14.2 — ‘the delay is only until I am released; then I shall reach home.’ Meaning: the timing of karma can be known.
3.23: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: friendliness and the rest (1.33) are sattvic dispositions (SK 23). Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 5.2 — ‘da: be compassionate’. Meaning: what one meditates on becomes one’s strength.
3.24: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the gross elements (SK 38) are shaped by the subtle. Veda: Atharvaveda 19.60 prays for strength in the arms, force in the thighs and firmness in the feet. Meaning: strength itself becomes an object of practice.
3.25: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 7 — things are unseen through subtlety, obstruction or distance; this power overcomes exactly those. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.12 — seen by ‘subtle seers’. Meaning: the Kārikā’s list of reasons for not seeing becomes a list of things to overcome.
3.26: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 53–54 describe the realms — divine, human, animal. Veda: Gāyatrī (Ṛgveda 3.62.10) — meditation on Savitṛ, the sun; Chāndogya Up. 3.1 — the sun as the honey of the gods. Meaning: the Vedic sun-meditation becomes a doorway to the worlds.
3.27: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: cosmic order, part of the manifest (SK 10). Veda: Ṛgveda 10.85 links the moon to Soma and the nakṣatras. Meaning: the Vedic sky-map becomes an object of meditation.
3.28: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the pole star (dhruva) as the fixed point among moving things. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.1.2 — the wise do not seek the fixed (dhruvam) among the unfixed. Meaning: the steady star is a picture of the steady Self.
3.29: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the arrangement of the body (SK 39 — the gross body born of parents). Veda: Atharvaveda 10.2.31 — ‘the city of the gods with eight wheels and nine gates’. Meaning: the Atharvaveda already mapped the body as a city with centres.
3.30: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: hunger and thirst belong to the body and prāṇas (SK 29). Veda: Chāndogya Up. 8.7.1 — the Self is ‘without hunger, without thirst’; Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 3.5.1 — the Self is beyond hunger and thirst. Meaning: the throat-centre touches what the Self already is.
3.31: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: steadiness from settling rajas (SK 13). Veda: Gītā 2.58 — like a tortoise drawing in its limbs, the wise one draws in the senses. Meaning: the tortoise image recurs because stillness is drawn inward.
3.32: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: light at the crown is sattvic radiance (SK 13). Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.3.16 and Chāndogya Up. 8.6.6 — one hundred and one channels of the heart; one rises to the crown, and going up through it one reaches immortality. Meaning: the Upaniṣads’ upward channel becomes a point of meditation.
3.33: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: prātibha, intuitive flash, is the sattvic peak of buddhi (SK 23: knowledge). Veda: Kena Up. 4.4 — Brahman ‘is like the lightning that flashes, like the blink of an eye.’ Meaning: knowledge can arrive all at once.
3.34: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the heart as the seat of buddhi. Veda: Chāndogya Up. 8.1.1 — ‘in this city of Brahman is a small lotus, a dwelling; within it a small space’; Atharvaveda 10.8.43 — ‘the lotus with nine gates, covered by three guṇas’, the earliest mention of three guṇas. Meaning: the Veda puts the Self in the heart; the yogi looks there.
3.35: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 20 and 37 — experience is failing to tell buddhi (sattva) from puruṣa. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.3.7 — ‘beyond the mind is sattva; beyond sattva the great self’; Ṛgveda 1.164.20 — one bird eats, the other watches. Meaning: experience is the confusion of the two birds.
3.36: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: subtle senses work on the tanmātras (SK 38). Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 3.19 — ‘without hands or feet it moves and grasps; without eyes it sees, without ears it hears.’ Meaning: perception without the usual instruments.
3.37: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 50–51 — even perfections can become a resting place. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.2.1–2 — the pleasant (preyas) blocks the good (śreyas). Meaning: powers are achievements outwardly and obstacles inwardly.
3.38: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 40–41 — the subtle body needs a support and can move between bodies. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.4.3 — like a caterpillar crossing from one blade to another, the self moves to a new body. Meaning: what moves at death can be moved in life.
3.39: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: udāna is one of SK 29’s five breaths. Veda: Praśna Up. 3.7 — ‘through one channel, udāna rising leads to the good world by merit’; Kaṭha Up. 2.3.16 — the channel to the crown. Meaning: Yoga takes the Upaniṣad’s up-breath and masters it.
3.40: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: samāna, the central breath (SK 29). Veda: Praśna Up. 3.5 — ‘samāna is in the middle; it evens out what is offered as food; from it rise the seven flames.’ Meaning: mastering samāna brings out the seven flames.
3.41: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: hearing arises from the sound-tanmātra, whose gross form is space (SK 38). Veda: Taittirīya Up. 2.1 — ‘from the Self arose space (ākāśa)’; Kena Up. 1.2 — ‘the ear of the ear’. Meaning: hearing and space share a root.
3.42: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the body made light by bringing it close to space (SK 38). Veda: Ṛgveda 10.136.4 — the long-haired muni ‘flies through the mid-air’; 10.136.2 — ‘the wind-girdled sages’. Meaning: the Ṛgveda’s earliest image of the ascetic is one who travels the air.
3.43: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: buddhi working outside the body loosens SK 39–41’s dependence on a support. Veda: Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 4.3.12 — in dream the immortal one ‘goes wherever he pleases’. Meaning: consciousness is not fenced in by the body.
3.44: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: gross, essence, subtle (tanmātra), pervasion (guṇa) and purpose — SK 38 and 12–13 read as five layers of each element. Veda: Taittirīya Up. 2.1 — space, air, fire, water, earth arising in order; Śvetāśvatara Up. 2.12 — ‘when the fivefold quality of yoga arises from earth, water, fire, air and space…’ Meaning: the elements are known from the inside.
3.45: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: the eight siddhis are power (aiśvarya), a sattvic form of buddhi (SK 23); SK 45 — ‘from power comes non-obstruction’. Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 2.12 — ‘no sickness, no ageing, no death for one with a body of yoga’s fire.’ Meaning: the Kārikā’s ‘non-obstruction’ is exactly the result listed here.
3.46: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: a perfected gross body (SK 39). Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 2.13 — ‘lightness, health, steadiness, clear complexion, a pleasant voice, a sweet smell’. Meaning: the Upaniṣad describes the same body.
3.47: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: grasping, essence, asmitā, pervasion and purpose — SK 24–27 trace the senses back to ahaṃkāra and the guṇas. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 2.3.6 — ‘knowing the separateness of the senses, the wise do not grieve.’ Meaning: senses are mastered by seeing what they are made of.
3.48: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: mastery of pradhāna — SK 11’s word for prakṛti. Veda: Śvetāśvatara Up. 1.10 — ‘pradhāna is perishable; the immortal imperishable is Hara’; 3.19 — moving without feet. Meaning: the yogi reaches the root of nature that Sāṃkhya names.
3.49: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 37 — only buddhi can discern the difference between pradhāna and puruṣa; SK 64 — and from that comes all-knowing. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 1.1.3 — ‘what is that, sir, by knowing which all this becomes known?’ Meaning: one distinction gives command of everything.
3.50: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 66 — the seen ceases to interest the seer; SK 68 — kaivalya. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.1.27 — Naciketas: ‘man is not satisfied by wealth.’ Meaning: dispassion even toward omniscience leaves only freedom.
3.51: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 50–51 — perfections are not the end. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.1.21–29 — Yama offers Naciketas celestial maidens, chariots and music; he says ‘keep them yourself.’ Kena Up. 3 — even the gods grew proud of their victory. Meaning: this sūtra is the Naciketas story as instruction.
3.52: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: moment and sequence — SK 9’s change seen at its finest grain. Veda: Kena Up. 4.4 — ‘like the blink of an eye’. Meaning: seeing change at the level of the instant shows what never changes.
3.53: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 37’s subtle distinction (sūkṣma antara) carried to the finest point. Veda: Kaṭha Up. 1.3.12 — ‘seen by the subtle seers with a subtle intellect.’ Meaning: discernment sharp enough to tell identical things apart.
3.54: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 64 — complete, pure, errorless knowledge. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 1.1.9 — ‘he who is all-knowing, all-wise’. Meaning: discriminative knowledge is ‘the deliverer’ (tāraka) because it carries across.
3.55: Sāṃkhya ↔ Yoga: SK 68 — kaivalya when prakṛti’s work is done; Yoga adds sattva’s purity equalling puruṣa’s. Veda: Muṇḍaka Up. 3.1.8 — the one of ‘purified sattva’ sees; Śvetāśvatara Up. 6.11 — ‘alone (kevala), without guṇas’. Meaning: when the mirror is perfectly clean, there is no more mistake about what is reflected.
